series: What to Check Before Launching a Cosmetics Brand

marketing.targetReader: Operators and compliance staff of Korean responsible cosmetics distributors using domestic OEM production
marketing.readerQuestion: Which training, reporting, quality, safety and registration-update duties continue after launch, and when?
ctaOutcomes: scope of separately agreed filing work

approvedBy: English draft based on the Korean card draft — source and user approval pending. Do not publish.

cards.headline: Registered as a cosmetics distributor. What's next?
body: The OEM factory makes your product, but your brand still has duties.
cards.promise: Know what to check and when
cards.takeaway: Training, reporting and product-quality duties continue after registration.
cards.design: Premium navy cover: an oversized calendar-clock illustration between a quality file and delivery icon; bold two-line headline, restrained cream accents.

cards.headline: Who keeps quality records after OEM production?

body.text: Manufactures and tests the cream, and supplies quality records as required by the law and contract.
As the responsible cosmetic distributor, keeps product specifications and quality records and oversees outsourced manufacturing and quality control.

cards.takeaway: Keep records identifying the actual batch—not just a factory's 'passed' message.
cards.design: Side-by-side cream panels: OEM factory and brand company, with a shared product-batch label between them; use a small file icon to anchor the record-keeping role.

cards.headline: Training and annual reports run on separate clocks

body.text: Initial manager training is due within 6 months of starting the role.
Refresher training is required once a year, based on the first training date.
Report prior-year production by end-February of the following year, even zero output if covered.

cards.takeaway: Check the manager's training record separately from the factory's annual output.
cards.design: Three large numeric modules on navy: 6 mo, 1/year and Feb; put each triggering date directly under its number rather than suggesting a single countdown.

cards.headline: Made 2,000. Sold 800. Which figure is reported?

body.text: Creams actually produced by the OEM factory
Creams sold to customers from that output

cards.takeaway: Production reports use actual output and production value, not just your online sales figures.
cards.design: Two horizontal bars drawn from zero, 2,000 versus 800 units; visually separate production records from checkout-sales data and preserve the true 2.5:1 proportion.

cards.headline: New batch, or changed ingredients?

body.text: If A001 and A002 differ only by batch number, and the reported ingredient list is unchanged, no new list report is needed.
If panthenol is added and the reported list changes, report the revised ingredients before that version is distributed or sold.

cards.takeaway: Compare the actual formula with the reported ingredient list, not just the batch number.
cards.design: Navy split view: identical cream jars marked A001/A002 on one side; revised ingredient sheet highlighting panthenol on the other.

cards.headline: One brand. Different compliance clocks.
body: Annual filings, ongoing records and event-driven duties follow different dates.
cards.design: Quiet cream break card: oversized statement and a thin horizontal rhythm line branching into annual, ongoing and event-triggered duties; generous whitespace.

cards.headline: A customer reports skin irritation. What next?

body.text: Record the product, batch number, timing and reported symptoms; inform the responsible manager.
Report serious adverse events and other covered urgent cases to MFDS within 15 days of learning.
Report in-scope, non-expedited safety information within 1 month after the half-year ends.

cards.design: A small customer-message card above a recorded batch label; below it, two clear routes for 15-day expedited and half-year routine safety reports.

cards.headline: Recall deadlines have different starting points

body.text: Due after learning the product is subject to recall
Recall period measured from the recall start
Recall period measured from the recall start

cards.takeaway: If legal recall applies, stop sales immediately and take necessary steps; extensions need grounds.
cards.design: Three bars for 5, 15 and 30 days: separate the first deadline (awareness of legal recall) from the other two (recall start) with distinct starting-point labels.

cards.headline: When company details change, check registration
head: Change
Check

body.text: Apply to update registration within 30 days of the change.
Check cosmetics registration apart from tax records.
Check suspension/closure filings and license-tax bills.

cards.takeaway: Pausing online sales does not automatically close the cosmetics registration.
cards.design: Dark navy document table with three rows and a subtle registration-certificate silhouette; highlight the 30-day rule only on the manager-change row.

cards.headline: Which company records should you check first?

body.text: Registration certificate, manager training records and recent production reports you already have.
Ethos Administrative Attorney Office can prepare registration-change documents; scope, fees and legally permitted filing work are agreed separately.

cards.takeaway: Send your records for a free preliminary review of duties, deadlines and missing documents.
cards.design: Premium navy close: document stack near the heading; two high-contrast cream panels for what the reader prepares and separately scoped paid administrative work; a single final review line.
